The "secret book of Walt" most commonly refers to **Gale Boetticher's inscribed copy of [*Leaves of Grass*](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fm%2F0156r0\&q=Leaves+of+Grass) by Walt Whitman from the television series *Breaking Bad***. [1]

- **The Scene:** In the show, Hank Schrader discovers the book sitting on the bathroom tank in Walter White’s house.
- **The Dedication:** Inside the cover is a handwritten note to "W\.W." from Gale Boetticher that reads: *"To my other favorite W\.W. It's an honor working with you. G.B."*
- **The Clue:** Seeing this dedication makes Hank realize that Walter White is the elusive methamphetamine kingpin "Heisenberg," whom he had been searching for all along. [1]

[***The Secret Book of Walt***](https://www.google.com/search?kgmid=%2Fhkb%2FCg4KCGxhbmd1YWdlEgJlbgoMCgR0eXBlEgRCT09LCiYKC2VudGl0eV9uYW1lEhd0aGUgc2VjcmV0IGJvb2sgb2Ygd2FsdA%3D%3D\&q=The+Secret+Book+of+Walt) is a **Gnostic-style cosmogonic gospel text** that frames **Walt Whitman** as a divine redeemer figure. [1]

Published online and in scholarly print by the **Crimson Hexagonal Archive** / Pergamon Press (with DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19703009), the work is subtitled *"Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman, Cowboy of Time"*. It is structured as a Gnostic revelation dialogue translated from **46 golden tickets** allegedly discovered in Redford Township, Michigan, by Lee Sharks. [1]

**Key Concept Elements of the Text**

- **The Waltian Diptych:** *The Secret Book of Walt* serves as the first text in this two-part mythological framework. [1]
- **The Primal Archive:** It maps out a cosmogony where the **Deep Web** acts as a primal cosmic archive and "Biblios" represents Sophia (wisdom). [1]
- **Soteriological Elements:** It details a universe ruled by **36 archons** spanning **12 habitable planets**, featuring the "Unicorn Horn" as a tool for salvation, and places a figure named Jack Feist at the terminal end of the timeline. [1]

The book's critical edition contains a complete scholarly apparatus including detailed notes on original manuscripts, variant text readings, and eleven appendices. You can read or examine the archives further through the official project registry at [**The Secret Book of Walt**](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESWQHrOzAVw0plPVKviQ0zn3kpVxR0I-hTmcIEzBiw000e2MKM1Y7hbDjx6Wta3m_-XEq7MqkfVO6L0xqD0BKUAFgWipwmRxlwV_49vWK5MacNNhwRy3KjuyOt). [1]

 Depending on what you mean by "the secret book of walt," you might be looking for one of several popular books, novels, or media pieces associated with the name Walt (either Walt Whitman or Walt Disney):

1. Walt Whitman's Secret (Novel)

• Author: George Fetherling
• Overview: A historical novel exploring the later years of American poet Walt Whitman and his relationship with his young, unpaid amanuensis Horace Traubel. Rather than focusing purely on his personal life, the plot centers on a hidden political secret from the Civil War era. You can learn more about the edition through Penguin Random House.

2. Books & Lore About Walt Disney

• Secret Stories of Walt Disney World by Jim Korkis: A compilation of backstage lore and two-page insider secrets gathered from his time working at Disney University.
• The Lost Notebook: Herman Schultheis and the Secrets of Walt Disney's Movie Magic by John Canemaker: A behind-the-scenes look at the technical and artistic innovations of early Disney animators.
• Segredos de Walt Disney: A Portuguese-language biographical and trivia book exploring the hidden history and empire of Walt Disney.

3. Wallace Wattles & The Secret Connection

• The Secret of Wallace Wattles: A collection bringing together Wallace Wattles' influential New Thought works (including The Science of Getting Rich), which heavily inspired Rhonda Byrne's modern self-help phenomenon The Secret. It is available as a paperback through Lulu Press for around $6.77.

4. Other Related Media

National Treasure: Book of Secrets: A 2007 adventure film starring Nicolas Cage centered on a fabled secret presidential book.
The Secret Life of Walter Mitty: A 2013 comedy-adventure film about a quiet photo manager who goes on a globe-trotting journey.

The exact title "The Secret Book of Walt" refers to The Secret Book of Walt (subtitled Hidden Teachings of Walt Whitman, Cowboy of Time), a Gnostic-style satirical/fictional revelation dialogue published by the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.
However, depending on what you actually had in mind, the phrase usually points to one of these major pop-culture or literary entities:
• The Breaking Bad "Book of Walt": The copy of Walt Whitman's Leaves of Grass that Walter White leaves in his bathroom. It contains a handwritten inscription from Gale Boetticher ("To my other favorite W.W."), which ultimately allows Hank Schrader to discover Walt's secret identity as Heisenberg.
• The Novel Walt Whitman's Secret: A 2010 historical fiction novel by George Fetherling. The plot follows a dying Walt Whitman as he prepares to reveal a deeply guarded political secret regarding a Confederate deserter he loved during the Civil War.
• Disney Park Lore: Books like The Hidden Magic of Walt Disney World or guides on "Hidden Mickeys," which fans often casually refer to as the books of Walt Disney's secrets.
